name: CRH PUBLIC LTD CO
business: Supplies aggregates, cement, concrete, asphalt, paving and infrastructure products to public infrastructure, commercial and residential construction customers, mainly in North America and Europe.

events.what: Agreement to acquire Arcosa for $150 per share cash, $8.5B EV, about $175M run-rate cost synergies by year three ($60M in year one); pending Arcosa stockholder and regulatory approval, close expected Q1 2027
events.source: document_id 52032 (announced 2026-06-22); 8-K 0001193125-26-276686 (EX-99.2 presentation, doc 72619); no Item 1.01/2.01 8-K returned

events.what: CFO appointed (internal) after Nancy Buese stepped down by mutual agreement 2026-05-11
events.from: CRH Americas Division CFO, Group Head of Finance

events.what: CFO appointed (external), replacing interim CFO Alan Connolly; departed after 12 months
events.from: Baker Hughes (EVP and CFO), previously Newmont CFO
CRH CFO and Chief of Staff to the CEO

next_event.source: Investor Day already held 2025-09-30 (document_id 52026) where the 2030 targets were set; next dated milestone found is the Arcosa close, expected Q1 2027 (document_id 52032)

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Level and year in the same metric (adjusted EBITDA margin 22% to 24% by 2030). CEO says Arcosa (over 21% EBITDA margin) is aligned with and accretive to margins.

statements.quote: We are targeting further margin expansion across our businesses with an adjusted EBITDA target of between 22% and 24% by 2030.
statements.speaker: Jim Mintern

statements.quote: The acquisition of Arcosa is fully aligned with the delivery of our 2030 financial targets, annual revenue growth of between 7%-9%, an adjusted EBITDA margin of 22%-24% by 2030, and average adjusted free cash flow conversion of over 100%.
statements.speaker: Jim Mintern

statements.quote: We currently expect approximately $175 million of run rate cost synergies to be achieved by year three. Here we have outlined the expected phasing with $60 million anticipated in the first year of ownership.
statements.speaker: Randy Lake

street.gap_assumption: Target midpoint 23.0% minus FY2030 consensus adjusted EBITDA margin 22.51% (11,320M / 50,297M), same metric. Consensus already sits inside the 22% to 24% range and 51 bps above its low end. Unknown whether brokers include Arcosa (pending). Calendar FY labels (December FYE).

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026], group adjusted EBITDA margin YoY as stated by CEO Mintern (docs 187765, 112107). Q2 2026 actuals not yet in VA, so LTM 20.4% is Q2 2025 to Q1 2026. FY2025 was the 12th consecutive year of margin expansion (+100 bps, doc 187766).

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: FY2030 consensus adjusted EBITDA margin is 22.51%, inside management's 22% to 24% by 2030 range and only 49 bps below the midpoint; hitting the midpoint adds just 2.2% to FY2030 consensus EBITDA. CRH is also not a low-margin laggard by its own history (12 straight years of expansion); stage 2 missed its CFO changes and the pending Arcosa deal.
verdict: Not the archetype: dated 22% to 24% EBITDA margin target by 2030 and a pending $8.5B Arcosa deal with $175M synergies, but the street already models 22.5% for 2030, the CEO is an internal 2025 successor, and A is only 1.
open_questions: Do FY2029 and FY2030 consensus include Arcosa, and does the deal plus $175M synergies push the street toward the 24% top end?
Why did external CFO Nancy Buese leave after 12 months, and does the internal successor change capital allocation?
Is the 36% drawdown a multiple de-rating on construction volumes rather than a margin problem?
